title: Punan Merap language - Wikipedia
text: Punan Merap (Mbraa) is a purported minor Austronesian language of Borneo in Indonesia. Soriente (2015) classifies Mbraa (also known as Merap) as a Kayan–Murik (Modang-Bahau) language.

title: Punan Merap Language (PUC) – L1 & L2 Speakers... | Ethnologue Free
text: Punan Merap is an endangered indigenous language of Indonesia. It belongs to the Austronesian language family. The language is used as a first language by all adults in the ethnic community, but not all young people.

title: Merap language — Grokipedia
text: The Merap language belongs to the Austronesian language family, specifically within the Malayo-Polynesian branch, and is classified as an endo-Bornean variety originating within the island of Borneo.
